meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is this?

examples.text: Что происходит? Я думала, что это доллары.
examples.trans: What is happening? I thought that those were dollars.

examples.text: И одного не оставляйте, чтобы по отелю не бродил.
examples.trans: And do not leave him alone, so he does not wander around the hotel.

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'исходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is happening', paired with 'произойти'.

examples.text: Что происходит? Я думала, что это доллары.
examples.trans: What is happening? I thought that those were dollars.
What is going on here?
What is going on?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Простите, я не успел поменять деньги.
examples.trans: Forgive me, I did not have time to exchange money.
Of course, here you go.

examples.text: Ладно, не плачь, сами счёт закроем.
examples.trans: Alright, do not cry, we will cover the bill ourselves.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'рвничать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be nervous, fret', paired with 'разнервничаться'.

examples.trans: Vika, do not be nervous.
I'm nervous too!
Don't be nervous, everything is fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы не знали, что этот люкс занят.
examples.trans: We did not know that this suite was occupied.
Excuse us for disturbing you.

examples.text: Комиссия в отеле. Мы сейчас уходим.
examples.trans: The commission is in the hotel. We are leaving right now.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'took, arrested', paired with 'брать'.

examples.text: Надо его выманить и без лишнего шума взять.
examples.trans: We need to lure him out and grab him without extra noise.
We caught the hypnotist.

examples.text: Костян, походу, мы не того взяли.
examples.trans: Kostyan, it looks like we grabbed the wrong guy.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hypnotist' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В отеле возможно появление мошенника и гипнотизёра.
examples.trans: The appearance of a fraudster and hypnotist in the hotel is possible.
The hypnotist is still in the hotel!

examples.text: Он же гипнотизёр! Он тебе в глаза посмотрит.
examples.trans: He is a hypnotist! He will look into your eyes.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: We will check everything right now!

examples.text: Комиссия в отеле. Мы сейчас уходим.
examples.trans: The commission is in the hotel. We are leaving right now.

examples.text: О, комиссия! Так я вам сейчас всё покажу.
examples.trans: Oh, the commission! Well I will show you everything right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'прашивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'interrogate, question', paired with 'допросить'.

examples.trans: We are interrogating him right now. Here are his things.
The police began to interrogate the witness.

examples.text: Если меня начнут допрашивать, я всё расскажу.
examples.trans: If they begin to interrogate me, I will tell everything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вчера клуб продул, вот он и психанул.
examples.trans: Yesterday the club lost, so he freaked out.
Here the little sofas are soft.
We are interrogating him right now. Here are his things.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'his', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Of course, here you go.

examples.text: Усатый в очках? Он в отеле живёт?
examples.trans: Moustached in glasses? Does he live in the hotel?

examples.text: Элеонора Андреевна просила меня за всем проследить.
examples.trans: Eleonora Andreyevna asked me to oversee everything.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thing' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We are interrogating him right now. Here are his things.
I've brought you your things.
Where are my things?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как выбрать хороший отель для отпуска?
examples.trans: How do you choose a good hotel for a vacation?
Or for a business trip?

examples.text: Специальная комиссия проверяет каждый уголок отеля.
examples.trans: A special commission inspects every corner of the hotel.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The victim is under hypnosis.

examples.text: Мне даже премию обещала, если всё хорошо пройдёт.
examples.trans: She even promised me a bonus if everything goes well.

examples.text: Витя, только ты меня можешь понять.
examples.trans: Vitya, only you can understand me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'told', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Я же сказала, не лезь не в своё дело!
examples.trans: I told you, do not meddle in what is none of your business!
What did you say?
Excuse me, where's the metro?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'meddle, interfere', paired with 'полезть'.

examples.text: Я же сказала, не лезь не в своё дело!
examples.trans: I told you, do not meddle in what is none of your business!
Don't jump the queue!
The cat is climbing the tree.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как выбрать хороший отель для отпуска?
examples.trans: How do you choose a good hotel for a vacation?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'one's own', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Какие номера у вас свободны, какие заняты?
examples.trans: Which rooms of yours are vacant and which are occupied?
At his workplace.

examples.text: Я же сказала, не лезь не в своё дело!
examples.trans: I told you, do not meddle in what is none of your business!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'business' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Or for a business trip?

examples.text: Погоди, а тебя комиссия вообще видела?
examples.trans: Wait, has the commission even seen you?

examples.text: Вы ещё не закончили? Вы очень медленно всё делаете.
examples.trans: Have you not finished yet? You are doing everything very slowly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Will this be enough?
What is this?

meanings.note: From Latin 'inspector' (observer, overseer, from 'inspicere', to look into).

examples.trans: This is an inspector from the commission!
Inspectors look for violations.

examples.text: Инспекторы ищут нарушения только ради денег.
examples.trans: Inspectors look for violations only for money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Wait, this is from the central office.

examples.text: В отеле возможно появление мошенника и гипнотизёра.
examples.trans: The appearance of a fraudster and hypnotist in the hotel is possible.
Will you measure the thickness of the carpet too?

meanings.note: From Latin 'commissio' (entrusting of authority, committee).

examples.text: Специальная комиссия проверяет каждый уголок отеля.
examples.trans: A special commission inspects every corner of the hotel.
No police! There is a commission in the hotel.
There is a commission in the hotel!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как выбрать хороший отель для отпуска?
examples.trans: How do you choose a good hotel for a vacation?
Right, we need to call the police.
You look simply lovely!

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'ключительный'). Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('exceptional').

examples.trans: Maxim, you are an exceptional idiot!

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень исключительный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very exceptional choice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'дурок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'jerk' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Maxim, you are an exceptional idiot!
There are only morons around!

examples.text: Вокруг меня одни лентяи и придурки!
examples.trans: Around me are only slackers and fools!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ходу').

examples.trans: Very funny! In my opinion, it looks like him.

examples.text: Костян, походу, мы не того взяли.
examples.trans: Kostyan, it looks like we grabbed the wrong guy.

examples.text: Да и вообще она не очень похожа на гипнотизёра.
examples.trans: And besides, she does not look much like a hypnotist.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What should we do now?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.text: Вы ещё не закончили? Вы очень медленно всё делаете.

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'вязывать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'untie'.

examples.trans: Untie him!
Untie him faster!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.text: А почему с ним пьёт ваш сотрудник?
examples.trans: And why is your employee drinking with him?

examples.text: Вы в порядке? А почему вы ругаетесь на этого милого человека?
examples.trans: Are you alright? And why are you yelling at this nice man?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'faster', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you, hurry!

We need fast internet.
